description: Vantaloc Space is a three person team of student builders taking on the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. We're building an interactive Moon and Mars outpost game that teaches kids how engineers balance life support, power, radiation shielding and food.
summary:
Lunar Life is a story game for kids that puts them in charge of a 14-sol mission on Mars. Players land, build a base and then face six real dangers: a dust storm, bad air, a solar storm, a marsquake, a hurt crewmate and a tense launch day. At each one they make a hard choice. Every option has a cost, and the game quietly tracks fuel, time and crew health. When the mission ends, they either fly home or get stuck on Mars, and a debrief shows which choices made the difference.

We built every danger on real science. The solar storms come from NASA’s DONKI space weather database, using the actual dates, speeds and strengths of storms that hit Earth and Mars. The facts come from missions like Curiosity, InSight, MAVEN and Perseverance, and each one links to its NASA source.

It matters because kids don’t learn space science by reading a list of facts. They learn it by caring about the people in the story. Here, radiation, dust and distance become problems kids have to solve, in English or Bangla.
details:
Lunar Life: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer
14 sols on Mars. 12 hard choices. Real NASA data. Can you bring your crew home?

Play: https://nasa-hack-26.pages.dev. Nothing to install and no sign-in. It runs on laptops, tablets and phones. Made by Vantaloc Space (team Binary Bandits) for kids aged 7 to 12, in English and Bangla.

The idea

  • The problem: Space science feels distant to kids. They read about radiation and dust storms, but don’t feel why astronauts care.
  • Our answer: Kids become the commander of a real-feeling Mars mission. Every danger is drawn from real NASA data, and every choice has a real cost.
  • The result: Kids don’t memorise facts. They use them to keep their crew alive.

What makes it stand out

  • Built on NASA data: the solar storms come from NASA’s DONKI database, with real dates, speeds (2,650 km/s) and strengths (Kp 9, 10 May 2024).
  • Choices that really matter: a hidden model tracks fuel, time and crew health. We tested all 4,096 possible paths. Only about 41% get home, and every one of the 12 decisions can change the ending.
  • Every fact is sourced: each fact card links to its NASA page (InSight, Curiosity, MAVEN, Perseverance/MOXIE, Opportunity, Phoenix, CHAPEA, NTRS). Automated tests check that the links are there.
  • A story kids want to finish: a crew with personalities (Mei the doctor, Tunde the engineer, Pip the robot) who chat, joke and get interrupted by disasters.
  • Learning after the ending: a debrief shows the one choice that flipped your ending, what each decision cost, your radiation dose against NASA’s career limit, and science cards on bones, eyes, isolation and radiation.
  • Two languages: full natural Bangla with Bangla numerals.
  • Accessible: read-aloud, Reduce motion, keyboard play, large text, sound on/off.
  • Zero tracking: no accounts, ads or analytics.

How the mission plays

  1. Arrival (sols 1–3): a documentary-style opening, picking a landing site, landing the craft yourself and building the base. Kids learn about distance, gravity, landing and what a base needs.
  2. Survival (sols 4–8): a planet-wide dust storm, CO₂ build-up and a solar storm that Earth warns about. Kids learn about solar power, air recycling, perchlorate, and radiation and shielding with water.
  3. The way home (sols 11–13): a marsquake cracks the fuel seal, then launch day. Kids learn about marsquakes, making fuel from Mars air (MOXIE) and launch windows.
  4. Ending and debrief (sol 14): Home or Stranded, then the mission report.

Tech stack

  • Language and framework: TypeScript, React 19 and Vite.
  • Art and sound: hand-coded SVG art and Web Audio sound. There are no image or sound files.
  • Testing: Vitest. 100+ tests cover balance across all 4,096 paths, fact sources and Bangla text.
  • Hosting: a static site on Cloudflare Pages, with no server or database.
  • Hardware: any modern browser.

Team: Vantaloc Space, NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
